text:
### Observed differences

- The dominant change is between two groups of activities. In the later window, A21, A22 and A23 each appear in about 79 in 100 traces (158 of 200), up from about 19 in 100 (37–38 of 200); A24, A25 and A26 each fall from about 82 in 100 (163–164 of 200) to about 21 in 100 (42 of 200) — a mirror-image shift of roughly 60 percentage points in opposite directions. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- A20, present in every trace in both windows, now routes to the first group: before, about 29 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A24, 29 to A26 and 24 to A25 (only about 3–9 to A21–A23); in the later window about 29 go to A23, 29 to A21 and 22 to A22 (only about 6–8 to A24–A26). [DIR003]
- The relational evidence flips in the same direction: A20 co-occurred with A21/A22/A23 in about 19 of 100 traces before versus about 79 of 100 after, with A20 preceding them in roughly 77–79 of those later cases; with A24/A25/A26, co-occurrence fell from about 82 to about 21 in 100. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- The groups' internal cohesion and their ties to other activities flip too: A21–A23 now appear together in about 79 of 100 traces (both internal orders roughly balanced, about 37–42 each) versus about 18–19 before, and now co-occur with A30 in about 79 of 100 (A21 first in about 44, interleaved in about 34); A24–A26 togetherness fell from about 82 to about 21 in 100, and they now typically appear without A30 (about 79 of 100 "A30 only"). Co-occurrence with A32/A33 rose to about 55 in 100 for A21–A23 and fell to about 15 for A24–A26. [REL015, REL016, REL023, REL036, REL037, REL041, REL020, REL027, REL033, REL038, REL042, REL045, REL021, REL022, REL039, REL040]
- Weaker, low-support changes around A10: its participation fell from about 17 to 7 in 100 traces, its position moved from a tight cluster near the end of the trace (median about 0.86) to earlier, far more variable positions (median about 0.36, measured in event positions), and its successors spread from almost always A33 (about 97%) to a flat mix (largest share about 21%); the A32-to-A10 gap also spread from mostly 1 step to 1–3 steps. These rest on only 33 versus 14 traces (4 for the lag). [POS001, DIR002, REL007, REL008, LAG001]
- A02 rose from about 2 to 9 in 100 traces with a fully redistributed successor profile, based on just 4 versus 18 traces. [OCC001, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the path following A20 changed: in the later window, the block A21–A23 (executed together in varying internal order, after A20 and alongside A30) runs in about four of five cases, whereas in the earlier window the block A24–A26 ran in about four of five cases in that role. [OCC002, OCC007, DIR003, REL009, REL012, REL020, REL038]

Supporting signs: the participation shift is about 60 percentage points in opposite directions (38 versus 158 traces per group), A20's successor shares flip consistently with full support in both windows, and the co-occurrence and ordering relations (A20 before the block, block members together, block alongside A30 and A32/A33) all move coherently, with every item exceeding about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits; 60 flagged items against roughly 0.9 expected if nothing had changed means the pattern as a whole is not what random splitting produces, although these items largely describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [DIR003, REL009, REL015, REL020, REL036]

Limitations: both groups are observed in both windows — A21–A23 already ran together in about 18–19 of 100 traces before, and A24–A26 still run together in about 21 of 100 after — and A20 already showed outgoing transitions to all six activities in the earlier window, so the evidence cannot distinguish a structural replacement from a flip in the selection probability between two pre-existing alternative blocks. [REL015, REL036, DIR003] The secondary changes around A10 and A02 rest on 18 or fewer later-window traces and may reflect sampling differences in variant frequencies rather than further structural change. [POS001, DIR002, OCC001, LAG001]
